annotations.text:
BURNING RUBBER — mobile redesign, v1 direction.

All screens are iPhone portrait 393×852. Top and bottom safe areas are left EMPTY on purpose — the real status bar and home indicator draw there, so nothing is painted underneath.

Palette and display type are lifted from the existing game: #F28D35 / #f77503 on near-black, Underdog for display. HUD numerals are Outfit.

OPEN DECISION — steering.

Everything here assumes DRAG: hold low on the screen, the car tracks your thumb. That assumption is what reserves the bottom 35%.

Tap-lanes or tilt would free that space and change the HUD layout. Settings shows all three as a picker, but one has to be the default.

THUMB ZONE — the rule these two screens obey.

No HUD element sits below y=554 (the bottom 35%). Score, coins, pause, power-up pills and the combo burst all live above it.

The car and the road still occupy that space — it is playfield, not chrome.

LANE MATH — worth checking against a real phone.

393pt ÷ 4 lanes = 98pt per lane, dividers at 98.25 / 196.5 / 294.75.

Every vehicle is now an original SVG drawn for this game, sized to a deliberate footprint — see artboard 11. Width is the number the engine must not drift from.

VEHICLE FLEET — replaces the 2019 sprites entirely.

The old cars were pulled off the internet six years ago and are not safe to ship in a store submission. These are drawn from scratch: 9 chassis, one body hex each, 68KB for the lot versus 8.4MB of PNGs.

Traffic varies by FOOTPRINT, not paint — that is what decides whether a gap is passable.
